theory.title: Verb + preposition + gerund
theory.explanation: Some verbs are followed by a specific preposition and then a gerund: apologise for doing, insist on doing, succeed in doing, complain about doing and think about doing. Learn each combination as a phrase.
theory.tip: Después de una preposición, usa el verbo en -ing.

content.passage: When a customer received the wrong order, the retailer apologised for making the mistake. The customer insisted on speaking to a supervisor and complained about waiting so long. The team succeeded in finding the correct item and arranged a new delivery. The manager thanked the customer for explaining the problem clearly and promised to review the checking process.

items.prompt: Describe a time a company apologised for making a mistake.
items.modelAnswer: When I buy something, I usually compare prices and read the conditions carefully. If there is a problem, I contact customer service and explain what has happened. I think a good company should listen to customers and offer a fair solution. I keep receipts and confirmation emails in case I need them later. Planning purchases helps me manage my budget and avoid unnecessary expenses.

content.audioTranscript: A: I'm calling about my order. B: Do you have the receipt? A: Yes. The customer service told me I could get a refund. B: Was there a problem with the delivery? A: Yes, so I asked to speak to the manager. B: I'll contact the supplier and check the payment. A: Thank you. Is the parcel going to the right address? B: Yes, it should arrive tomorrow.
